items.titleEn: TPG Eyes Take-Private Deal for BILL Holdings Within Days
items.summaryEn: Private equity group TPG is likely to reach a take-private deal for BILL Holdings within days, the Financial Times reported Tuesday (Nov. 17), citing unnamed sources. items.titleEn: Gold struggles near one-year lows, silver rebounds as stocks slide, Fed hike bets persist - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were little changed in late U.S. trading Tuesday, while silver rebounded from Monday's sharp losses as weaker U.S. economic data, declining Treasury yields and renewed geopolitical tensions competed with expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. Gold struggled to sustain gains despite a weaker dollar and another broad equity market selloff, while silver attracted bargain hunting after its recent decline. Spot gold was trading near $3,853.10 an ounce, down $2.40, or 0.06%, while spot silver was trading near $47.330, up $0.472, or 1.01%, on the session. Gold traded between $3,836.00 and $3,891.60 during the day, while silver's range extended from approximately $46.710 to $48.130. Tuesday's U.S. economic reports provided further evidence of uneven growth as elevated borrowing costs and persistent inflation continued to pressure consumers and industrial activity. October retail sales increased 0.2%, matching expectations but slowing substantially from September's 0.8% advance. Sales excluding automobiles rose 0.6%, above expectations for a 0.4% increase, suggesting underlying spending remained comparatively resilient. Industrial production declined 0.4% in October, substantially below expectations for a 0.1% increase, following September's 0.7% gain. Manufacturing output increased 0.3%, while mining production fell 0.8% and utilities output declined 4.3%. Capacity utilization slipped to 76.4%. The mixed figures reinforced concerns about slowing economic momentum without providing sufficient evidence that inflation pressures have eased enough to alter the Fed's tightening trajectory.

items.titleEn: Nvidia stock rises after hours as revenue forecast beats estimates
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA. The January-quarter revenue guide of ~$130B (vs ~$125.3B expected) plus ~71.5% gross margin confirms AI chip demand is holding up even with CEO turnover. Record buybacks ($28.1B in the quarter; $62B YTD) add downside support and signal confidence in cash generation. Key Risk: A sharp AI-spend slowdown that forces Nvidia to cut guidance again, wiping out the margin and growth confidence. Sell AMD. If Nvidia’s forecast beat is sustained, it reinforces Nvidia’s share and pricing power in AI accelerators and systems, making AMD’s AI ramp harder to monetize. The market will likely reward the clear leader while punishing laggards when guidance is the key catalyst.
